page: Microsoft Azure DC2as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DCASv5 series, hosted via Microsoft Hyper-V. The server configuration features an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor offering 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads. Memory allocation sits at 8.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AES, VAES, SHA_NI, AVX, BMI2, and FMA. There are no attached graphics processors, and the instance provisions without local storage, necessitating external storage configurations.

Benchmark results demonstrate adequate baseline execution on single-threaded tasks alongside capacity constraints on concurrent processing. Single-core performance indicators, including a stress-ng score of 2002.86 and a Geekbench single-core result of 1198.0, place the instance within the average median range. However, multi-core outputs reveal limited total throughput due to the dual-thread core ceiling, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 1449.0, a PassMark CPU score of 2397.17, and a clang software compilation mark of 1662.0, all ranking in the lower tiers. Cryptographic throughput on PassMark registered at 1459.06, supported by hardware SHA and AES instructions, while Redis SET operations achieved 1.7 million operations per second.

With its minimal compute footprint and lack of bundled local storage, the DC2as_v5 offers an entry-level operational profile suitable for modest, consistent workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation avoids burstable throttling, but the limited 2-thread architecture restricts parallel computing potential. This instance is best aligned with lightweight application services, staging environments, internal tooling, basic proxy layers, and microservices with moderate memory needs.
description: Microsoft Azure DC2as_v5 is a general-purpose instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core, 8.0 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core), and 32 MB of L3 cache. The architecture incorporates hardware cryptographic features including AES, VAES, and SHA extensions, but does not provide onboard local storage or GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the DC2as_v5 demonstrates median-tier single-core performance with a stress-ng score of 2002.86 and Geekbench single-core score of 1198.0, while aggregate multi-core results such as the PassMark CPU score of 2397.17 reflect the bounds of a dual-thread system. This virtual machine is suitable for entry-level workloads, lightweight backend microservices, basic testing environments, and low-traffic utility tasks requiring dedicated general-purpose resources.
